summary.intent: Create the Phase 60 PLAN.md for CipherBox's IPNS verification cross-layer closeout, covering desktop verified-resolve, API hot-path caching, and a strict-equality first-publish cutover.
summary.outcome: Completed research and decision-making; produced CONTEXT.md with 12 locked decisions and the full 14-branch/7-producer change-site inventory. Actual planner spawn (PLAN.md generation) had not started by transcript end.

repo: The embedded sequence in IPNS records lives inside the signed CBOR blob covered by the V2 signature, not the plaintext protobuf field-5 copy — you cannot change it on a live record without re-signing with the Ed25519 key.
The API server cannot re-sign IPNS records: it stores only ECIES-wrapped keys and has no signing primitive (no createIpnsRecord/signEd25519 anywhere in apps/api/src).

TEE republish does increment the embedded sequence (+1) and persists it via syncFolderIpnsSequence — natural rollover drains enrolled embedded-0 records to embedded-2 within one 6-hour cycle. One workflow subagent incorrectly claimed TEE re-signs at the same sequence (conflated the upsertFolderIpns idempotent-republish branch with the actual TEE cron path).

You cannot identify embedded-0 live records by filtering folder_ipns.sequence_number = 0: the API hard-codes first-publish DB sequence to '1' and a historical backfill already normalized 0→1. The only authoritative check is decoding the signed_record CBOR directly.
The initial todo named only 3 embed-0 producer sites; the audit found 7 total. The two useAuth.ts sites (vault-key blob + root folder) fire on every new web vault and are the highest-impact omission.
resolve_ipns_verified lives in cipherbox-fuse, not cipherbox-sdk — closing the SDK unverified bypasses requires a new verified wrapper in api-client or moving the chokepoint.
Neither Rust nor TS verifier checks record EOL/expiry on resolve; a validly-signed expired record passes both.

code.finding: build_cbor_data embeds the sequence inside the signed CBOR; compute_v2_signature at line 220 covers it — changing embedded sequence requires full re-sign.
Skew allowance: seq_ok = embedded_seq == resp_seq || (resp_seq == 1 && embedded_seq == 0). Drop the disjunct for strict cutover.
Embeds sequence 0 on folder create: create_ipns_record(&ipns_key_arr, &value, 0, 86_400_000). Must change to 1.
Identical embed-0 first-publish producer to mkdir.rs — must also be changed to 1.
FUSE bin first publish: make_bin_record(0), gated on is_first_bin_publish at line 555. Also embeds 0.
Two embed-0 first-publish sites on vault init: vault-key blob (191) and root folder metadata (208). Highest-impact producer omission — fires on every new web vault.
Vault settings first publish stays at sequenceNumber: 0n when no prior record resolves (catch at line 116 leaves it 0n).
SDK vault-key blob first publish embeds sequence 0. The one embed-0 site the todo explicitly named.
TS skew disjunct (resp==1n && embedded==0n) at 285; legacy no-signature else branch at 293 returns cid with signatureVerified:false — no consumer reads the flag.
All-3-fields-absent returns Ok(None) — legacy fail-OPEN. For strict cutover, this must return Some(false) instead.
Calls resolve_ipns directly with zero verification — accepts tampered CID. Unverified bypass not mentioned in the original todo.
Second unverified resolve_ipns call in the SDK — same bypass as registry.rs.
Row with signed_record IS NULL returns cid+seq HTTP 200 (unverifiable legacy). Must return null → 404 for strict cutover.
First-publish gate accepts embedded in {0n,1n}. Must drop 0n to reject embed-0 records at source after producer sites are fixed.
TEE republish increments: newSequenceNumber = BigInt(entry.sequenceNumber) + 1n, then re-signs. Enrolled embedded-0 records self-heal to embedded-2 on next cycle.

workflow: Running a blast-radius recon workflow before committing to a phase scope surfaces omissions (7 producer sites vs 3) that would have caused regressions if the plan had started from the todo alone.

No-production-instance context dramatically simplifies a migration decision: wiping staging + bootstrapping fresh eliminates the entire drain-pass concern, collapsing a conditional go/no-go into a clean unconditional rip-out.
When a recon workflow produces contradictory subagent findings, a targeted source-read (TaskOutput → Read the output file) is needed to resolve which finding is authoritative before acting.

friction: The original todo scope was materially incomplete — 3 producer sites documented, 5 more found by audit, with the two highest-impact sites (useAuth.ts vault init) not mentioned at all.
One recon subagent gave a wrong answer about TEE republish behavior (claimed idempotent re-sign at same sequence) — required a second recon pass and direct source verification to correct.
The transcript ends mid-workflow (CONTEXT.md written, planner not yet spawned), so the session did not reach the plan or verification loop stages.
open_items: Spawn gsd-planner against the CONTEXT.md to produce the actual PLAN.md task breakdown for Phase 60.
Design and implement a verified-resolve wrapper in crates/api-client so crates/sdk can close the unverified resolve bypasses without taking a dependency on cipherbox-fuse.
Decide how to handle the SDK unverified bypass scope sizing — the recon flagged it as extra scope not in the original proposal.
Add resolve-side expiry/EOL checking to both Rust and TS verifiers (intentionally deferred by the user to this phase but not yet planned).
Regenerate the cross-language test vector (tests/vectors/ipns/verify.json) after reclassifying legacy-absent and first-publish-skew cases from valid/legacy to invalid.

Audit whether the SDK vault-key blob embed-0 site (vault/index.ts:44) needs a separate fix path from the folder producers — it was the one the todo named but its record type may flow through different API gates.
